who_can_apply: School year: students who have started 10th grade or are at least 16. Summer: students at least 14.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online Junior Application. Contact Chasity Drees. Chasity Drees is the Volunteer Coordinator. Email cdrees@altru.org. Or call 701.780.5125.
notes: The page does not mention shots or background checks. Ask the coordinator what is needed before you start.
duration: At least one shift a week, 2 to 4 hours, for at least one semester.
pay_detail: Unpaid.

who_can_apply: Youth in 8th through 12th grade, both 4-H members and non-members. Check the program page for exactly how grade level is counted.
how_to_apply: Register in 4-H Online and pick a session track. Fill out the financial help form by the same date if you need it.
notes: Tracks in 2026 were Choose Your Adventure, Animal Science Roundup, MVP Leadership, Mission Moon and Horticulture. Cancel by June 1 for a full refund. After that there are no refunds.
duration: 3 days (June 23 to 25 in 2026)
pay_detail: $260 for 4-H members and $275 for non-members in 2026. Financial help is offered.

who_can_apply: High school students entering their junior or senior year. The page says 'All students are welcome.'
how_to_apply: Fill out the Summer 2027 Interest Form on the page. It tells you when applications open. Then register online. You ask for financial help on the registration form.
notes: The page only says applications open 'in January'. No exact opening day is known. Dates are marked tentative on the page.
duration: One week. Tentative 2027 sessions: July 11 to 15 and July 18 to 22.
pay_detail: The page lists $450 through June 26 or $500 for late registration (this may be last year's price). It covers housing, meals, a t-shirt and on-campus costs. You can ask for financial help on the registration form.

who_can_apply: Middle and high school students who enjoy hands-on learning, per the program page. One camp is for middle and high school students. The other camps listed are for 3rd to 6th graders.
how_to_apply: Use the sign up link for your camp on the program page. Questions? Email workforcedevelopment@msubillings.edu. Or call 406-896-5965.
notes: The page does not say which year the dates are for. Check before you plan.
duration: One week, Monday to Friday. Middle and high school camp dates on the page: July 27-31
pay_detail: $250 per student. Drone equipment and materials are included.

who_can_apply: Youth in school, ages 14 to 21, who have low income and at least one barrier from the state list. Youth out of school, ages 16 to 24, can also qualify under other rules. The barriers include a disability, foster care and no home. Being behind in basic skills is also a barrier.
how_to_apply: The state page has no application form. It points to a provider list. For Billings, the May 2026 list names District VII HRDC, contact Kelly Marquardt, 406-247-4788, kmarquardt@hrdc7.org.
notes: Other providers on the May 2026 state list: Missoula District XI HRDC (Lynda Schuldheisz, 406-728-3710) and Opportunities, Inc. in Great Falls (Jeff Beisecker, 406-761-8462). Only some teens qualify. Ask the provider first.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Paid and unpaid work experience are both listed. Pay rates are not stated.

who_can_apply: High school students. The program page does not state an age or grade rule beyond that.
how_to_apply: Fill out the application form linked on the program page. For questions call the center at 406-294-5099.
notes: Training is mandatory. The page does not list fall session dates. The center is at 7026 S Billings Blvd.
duration: Spring 2026 session: training March 26, then Thursdays 3:30 to 5:15 PM, April 2 to May 21
pay_detail: Volunteer role. Pay and service hours are not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: High school students with a documented disability, an IEP or a 504 plan. The summer camp is limited to 30 students. The page does not list grades or ages.
how_to_apply: The page does not list student steps. Schools that want to take part should contact Richie Solomon at 406-657-2092 or richard.solomon@msubillings.edu.
notes: If you do the campus visits in the school year, you get into the summer camp if you want to go.
duration: Four-day summer camp each June
pay_detail: Free. Tuition, fees, books, lodging and meals are covered for accepted camp students.

who_can_apply: Students at Senior, Skyview, West, Hardin or Lockwood high schools who finished 8th grade, are a U.S. citizen or permanent resident, and want to go to college. Your parents must not have a four-year degree, and your family must meet income rules. The page does not list the income limits.
how_to_apply: Get a paper application from the Upward Bound staff. Return it to your school counselor or mail it in. Eligible students get an interview. Phone: 406-657-2116. Email: upwardbound@msubillings.edu.
notes: Students not selected go on a waiting list. Selection looks at grades, recommendations and the interview. The program page does not say if the summer program is free. The summer page says students can get a stipend of up to $90.
duration: Six weeks in summer plus school-year advising
pay_detail: Free. Summer students can get a stipend of up to $90.

who_can_apply: Most positions need you to be at least 15 years old. Lifeguards must hold a lifeguard certification.
how_to_apply: The page does not describe the steps. It links job descriptions and a lifeguard course sign-up. Call 406-969-3131 to ask when hiring opens.
notes: 2026 lifeguard training weekends were May 1-3, May 8-10, May 15-17 and May 22-24, limited to the first 10 sign-ups. The program page does not say whether training will be held next spring.
duration: Summer season. Start and end dates are not stated.
pay_detail: The page says pay is competitive but gives no hourly number. The $150 lifeguard certification fee is paid back after one month of work.

who_can_apply: Youth. The program page does not state an age or grade rule.
how_to_apply: Use the Sign Up Here link on the program page. It opens the YDAT volunteer site for Billings. Make an account, then sign up for projects. A parent can set up a profile for each child. Phone: 406-657-8371.
notes: The program page does not list ages, dates or hour rules. Call the parks office to ask what ages can join.
duration: Project by project
pay_detail: Volunteer program. Pay is not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Teens. Age or grade rules are not stated on the program page.
how_to_apply: Apply through the library's Teen Advisory Board page. The page says to contact hoys@billingsmt.gov for more information. The main library phone is 406-657-8258.
notes: The library's volunteering page says no new volunteers are being taken now. Ask if they take late applications.
duration: School year (2026-2027), meeting the first and third Wednesday of each month at 4:30 p.m. in the CO+LAB
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 and older.
how_to_apply: The page does not list steps. Email Kaylinn at kaylinn@wisewonders.org to start.
notes: The museum job page says there are no open jobs now. It asks people to send a resume and cover letter to info@wisewonders.org for future jobs.
duration: Hours are not stated on the program page
pay_detail: Volunteer role. No pay is mentioned on the program page.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 18. You must apply.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Google Form on the program page. Questions? Contact Angel Shandy, Museum Art Educator. Call 406-256-6804 ext. 238. Or email arteducator@artmuseum.org.
notes: The page does not give a year for the Spring dates; they are listed under Spring 2027. The page does not say how many service hours you get.
duration: Meets the 1st and 3rd Wednesday of each month, 3:30 to 5 PM
pay_detail: Free to join. The program page does not mention pay or a stipend.

who_can_apply: Members are youth ages 9 to 19 (a 19-year-old must still be in high school). Ages are counted on October 1.
how_to_apply: Find a club on the county club list. Contact the club leader first, because the leader must approve you. Then enroll online with the link on the county 4-H page. Extension office: 406-256-2828.
notes: Some clubs have waiting lists. The $25 fee is paid to the club.
duration: 4-H year starts October 1
pay_detail: Member fee is $25. Most shooting sport projects cost $15 more per discipline.

who_can_apply: High school students and recent graduates, ages 16 to 19 (from the 2024 report).
how_to_apply: The program page does not describe a student sign-up. Contact Big Sky Economic Development in Billings to ask how to join.
notes: Based on an August 2024 report that says 34 students finished in 2024. Ask Big Sky Economic Development if the program still runs.
duration: One summer
pay_detail: Paid positions. The wage is not stated.

who_can_apply: Each job lists its own minimum age, 14 or 15. Lifeguards need Lifeguard, First Aid and CPR certification. The page says 'FREE training if you join our team!'
how_to_apply: Fill out the BPRD Job Application PDF in Adobe Reader (not in your web browser). Lifeguards also fill out the Aquatic Application Supplement Form. Email to jobs@bisparks.org or drop off or mail to 400 E. Front Ave., Bismarck, ND 58504.
notes: The page lists the season dates without a year. Park maintenance and some other jobs are for older workers. North Dakota work rules for minors were not checked.
duration: Varies. Youth basketball runs Oct 26 to Jan 16. Open Gym Supervisor is Nov to March on weekend afternoons. BLAST leader is 15 to 20 hours a week after school. Arena attendant is 25 to 30 hours a week.
pay_detail: Paid. Pay rates are not listed on the program page. Employees get a benefits pass for golf, pool and fitness.

who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 17. You must be 13 by June 1.
how_to_apply: The page does not describe the steps. Contact Erica Carnes at elcarnes@blankparkzoo.net or 515-974-2543. Hours count toward the Silver Cord award.
notes: You and your parents choose your shifts, and once you sign up you are expected to attend. Volunteering cannot start until the fee is paid.
duration: Primarily June, July and August. First-year teens must log at least 40 hours before December 31.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Teens pay a fee: $35 for zoo members or $40 for non-members. It covers a t-shirt, training and an online manual, and is due before orientation.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 and up. If you are under 18, you can do Education Support, Group Volunteering and Community Engagement. Event Support is for ages 18 and up. Education Support and Community Engagement need a ride you can count on. They also need a background check.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online volunteer form on the program page. Send questions to dcivolunteer@dcidaho.org.
notes: Event Support is listed for ages 18 and up on the program page. Parent permission rules are not stated on the program page.
duration: About 6 to 12 hours a month on a regular day and time. Shifts are 2 hours, between 9:30 AM and 4:30 PM.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role

who_can_apply: Student Service is for grades 7 to 12. Long-term volunteering is open to ages 12 to 17 with a pre-approved adult who volunteers with you. The Student Service Mentor path is for ages 14 and up after 3 sessions in a semester.
how_to_apply: Use the Register Now button on the program page for grades 7 to 12. You must register for each session. For long-term volunteering, teens under 18 must volunteer with a pre-approved adult, and only the adult can handle animals.
notes: Sessions meet at the Education Center, 1300 S Bird Street, Boise. Parents do not have to stay. Phone 208-342-3508.
duration: Short sessions. Long-term volunteers sign up for at least 6 months.
pay_detail: Short sessions cost $15 each. Scholarships are available. Homeschool groups pay $40 per group.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 16 through 24. You must be a U.S. citizen or eligible to work in the U.S., meet residency and low-income rules (with a few exceptions), and need help as shown by one of six factors. You must bring papers that prove you qualify.
how_to_apply: Contact your local Idaho Department of Labor office. Or ask for a visit with the online form on the program page. Bring papers such as a birth certificate, Social Security card or pay stubs.
notes: Boise office: 317 W. Main St., 1st Floor East, phone 208-332-3575. The program page lists a Caldwell office at 208-364-7781 and no Nampa office.
duration: Not stated on the program page
pay_detail: Paid and unpaid work experience is listed. Pay rates are not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Teens and young adults. High school students are especially encouraged. You need a picture ID and a Social Security card, and 12 hours a week for 8 weeks. Exact ages: not stated on the program page.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online form. Use the Apply Now button on the program page.
notes: Call 208-377-2613 (the number in the page footer) to ask about the Treasure Valley wait list. Email youthworks@youthranch.org to ask about acceptable documents. The program page does not give a reopening date.
duration: 8 weeks, 12 hours per week
pay_detail: $720 stipend, paid when you finish the program (12 hours a week for all 8 weeks, plus the Week 8 workshops)

who_can_apply: You must be at least 15 before the last class session. On day one you must pass two swim tests: a swim-tread-swim sequence without stopping to rest, and a timed event within 1 minute, 40 seconds. The city-run lifeguard classes are for current and future City of Boise employees only.
how_to_apply: Apply for the pool job on the city job postings. The link is on the Pools and Aquatics page. Then register for a city lifeguard course. The page says other lifeguard classes listed on it are open to the public.
notes: The Teen Activities page also lists summer jobs at pools and playcamps. They hire ages 15 and up, and rides are provided. It also lists a Youth Employment Program for grades 9 to 12. That one hires ages 14 and up. The pages give no details.
duration: Summer pool season; classes in winter and spring
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Incoming high school juniors and seniors of the 2027-28 school year. Limited to 50 students, first come first served.
how_to_apply: Join the waitlist on the camp page to get registration alerts. Registration opens in January.
notes: Spots are first come, first served, so join the waitlist for alerts early.
duration: 3 days, June 15 to 17, 2027
pay_detail: $395 for 2027. The page says meals, breaks and snacks are provided and students stay two nights in a dorm.

who_can_apply: Students currently in 9th, 10th or 11th grade (ages 14 to 17). Only 50 students are chosen.
how_to_apply: Apply when the application opens in early 2027. Chosen students get an email by mid May saying they have a spot. Questions: visitCOEN@boisestate.edu or 208-426-2688.
notes: The camp page does not list camp dates or the steps of the application. Watch the page in early 2027.
duration: Overnight camp (length and dates not stated on the program page)
pay_detail: Free to attend. It is not a paid job.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 15 to 18 from Boise and the Treasure Valley who like water and climate topics. You must be able to give the required hours.
how_to_apply: The program page has no application link right now. Email WaterShed@CityOfBoise.org or call (208) 608-7309 to ask about the next round.
notes: Interview steps are not stated on the program page. The WaterShed is at 6411 N. Ancell Ave, Boise.
duration: Training in the first week of June, then 5 hours every Wednesday (9 AM to 2 PM) until school starts in August. Some evenings and weekends, and year-round work is possible.
pay_detail: Paid position. The hourly pay is not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: The page says many roles are open to applicants 14 years and older. Some positions need applicants to be 16 or 18 and up. Each job posting lists its own age.
how_to_apply: Apply online only through the city's governmentjobs.com site (CityOfCR.com/SeasonalJobs). You can apply for more than one role. Lifeguard classes run monthly through May. Questions about lifeguard age and class fees: pools@cedar-rapids.org.
notes: The lifeguard age and the class fee refund are not stated on the program pages. Ask pools@cedar-rapids.org. Past job fairs were in winter, so watch the page from January. Iowa work paper rules were not checked.
duration: Varies by job. The page says positions vary by age, schedule and season length.
pay_detail: Lifeguards start at $15.00 an hour. Swim lesson instructors (WSI) start at $16.00 an hour. Other pay is not listed.

who_can_apply: High school students who meet one or more rules, such as being an Idaho resident or attending an Idaho high school, or being 16. Sophomores who are not yet 16 on the first day of class need an age waiver. Homeschool students can join if they meet the same age or grade level.
how_to_apply: Fill out the interest form to hold a spot on the waiting list. Go to the information meeting. Then finish official registration and send your transcript and test scores.
notes: Classes meet in person on the Idaho Falls campus. Hours were 8:30 am to 1:00 pm. Check the page next spring to see if the program returns.
duration: 8 weeks, Tuesday to Thursday mornings (June 2 to July 23 in 2026)
pay_detail: Free. All student costs are covered by grants, scholarships or state funding. Earn 5 to 6 college credits.

who_can_apply: Teens must be 14 years old. The page says you will be asked to show proof of age.
how_to_apply: Get the application on the volunteer page. It is in the Bismarck section. The Volunteer Coordinator is Tanya Olheiser. The phone number is (701) 530-7159. The email is tanya.olheiser@commonspirit.org.
notes: The page does not list the service areas, shots or background checks for teens. Ask the coordinator.
duration: Set hours not listed. Teen shifts are available after school, and weekend shifts vary by location.
pay_detail: Unpaid.

who_can_apply: Middle and high schoolers ages 13 to 17 as of June 1. Each member needs an individual or family zoo membership and an up-to-date tetanus shot.
how_to_apply: To apply, call (701) 223-7543 ext. 3. Or send an email to educate@dakotazoo.org. Ask for the volunteer coordinator.
notes: Ask the zoo when the next sign-up opens.
duration: Summer. At least 12 hours in June and July and 5 hours in August. Monthly meetings on the first Tuesday, 6 to 7 pm.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Teens buy an $11 Zoo Crew t-shirt and need a zoo membership. The membership price is not listed on the program page.

who_can_apply: Kids can volunteer from age 10. Those under 17 must have a parent or guardian with them during their shift. Teens who are 17 can volunteer with a parent or guardian's signature.
how_to_apply: Fill out the volunteer application on the shelter website. Some roles, such as the Litter-ary Club, need orientation first. Email the volunteer team with questions.
notes: The shelter can verify hours for the Silver Cord award. Ages 10 to 16 cannot come alone. A parent or guardian must stay for the whole shift. Questions: volunteer@arl-iowa.org.
duration: Not stated on the program page
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role

who_can_apply: Students currently enrolled in high school. The application asks for your grade, 9th through 12th.
how_to_apply: Apply online on the program page. Answer the essay questions. Six of them must be filled in. Upload five pieces of your art. Questions: studioclasses@desmoinesartcenter.org.
notes: A class, not a job. Next dates not posted.
duration: Nine months, once a week, following the school calendar.
pay_detail: Tuition is not listed on the program page. Ask the Studio Arts Department. The Art Center offers help with travel costs for students who need help getting to class.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 and up for an ongoing volunteer role. The event volunteer form is for people who will not volunteer on a regular basis. Age rules for event volunteers: not stated on the program page.
how_to_apply: If a job looks good to you, fill out a volunteer form. There is one for ongoing roles and one for events. Both are on the program page.
notes: The program page says the event form is a good fit for Silver Cord volunteer programs but does not explain that program. The page lists no contact name, phone or email.
duration: Ongoing, or short event shifts. Hours per week are not stated on the program page.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role

who_can_apply: High school students who are current juniors or younger. Graduating seniors cannot join. Priority goes to the classes of 2027 and 2028. Classes with prerequisites need those finished first.
how_to_apply: Fill out a pre-registration form for each class. You can take up to two classes. Seats depend on space and placement is not promised. For classes at Central Campus or Valley High School, do not send the form. Contact the Coordinator for that program.
notes: Campuses listed for 2026 were Ames, Ankeny, Perry, Des Moines (Urban), West Des Moines, and online. Students are expected to attend when the class begins. Call (800) 362-2127 with questions.
duration: Courses run from late May through early August. In 2026 they ran from May 26 to August 5.
pay_detail: No cost to the student. Books and supplies are provided before the first day of class.

who_can_apply: Students entering grades 9 to 12 in 2026-2027, or 2025 and 2026 high school graduates, who are interested in healthcare, math or science. Ages: not stated on the program page.
how_to_apply: Register online with the link on the program page and pay by the deadline. Questions go to Taylor Burgraff at taylor.burgraff@drake.edu or 515-271-1823.
notes: Meals are in the Hubbell Dining Hall. Spots are forfeited if payment is not made by the deadline. No refunds after the deadline.
duration: 3 days and 2 nights in a campus residence hall (July 9 to 11 in 2026)
pay_detail: $200 per student. Financial help may be available for students who qualify.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 24, in or out of school. You must be a U.S. citizen, permanent resident, or someone lawfully admitted to the U.S. The program serves youth who face big barriers to jobs or more school.
how_to_apply: Register on IowaWORKS.gov. Then call or visit your local IowaWORKS office to meet with a career planner who checks if you qualify. You can also fill out the Workforce Services Form on the program page.
notes: The program page does not list local office addresses or phone numbers. Iowa Workforce Development is at 1000 East Grand Avenue, Des Moines, IA 50319.
duration: Not stated on the program page. Follow-up help lasts at least 12 months after you finish, as needed.
pay_detail: Paid and unpaid work experiences are listed. Pay rates are not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Age 14 by June 1 and no older than 18, entering grade 9 or above in the fall. A parent or guardian must sign the application. Teens who turn 18 during camp need a background check.
how_to_apply: Fill out the application. A parent or guardian must also sign it. Go to a 1-hour group interview. If accepted, attend a 3-hour training and then sign up for your weeks.
notes: Summer camp runs 9 to 4, Monday to Friday, from June to mid-August. Questions: daycamp@lhf.org.
duration: At least 2 weeks for new junior counselors, scheduled 8:30 to 4:15, Monday to Friday
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role. Hours may count toward a school Silver Cord award, so check with your school.

who_can_apply: The lifeguard class is for ages 15 and up. The page does not state an age rule for the jobs themselves. Call the department to ask about camp staff and other seasonal jobs.
how_to_apply: Register for the lifeguard class with the Register Here link on the city Aquatics page. Apply for jobs through the Park Jobs link on the same page. Questions: parks@dmgov.org or (515) 237-1386.
notes: The Dec 4 to 6 class date is shown without a year on the program page. Iowa work paper rules for teens were not checked. Summer camp staff jobs may have a higher age limit, so confirm before you apply.
duration: Lifeguard jobs at the indoor pool are year-round. The class meets Friday to Sunday.
pay_detail: Paid jobs. Pay is not listed on the program pages. The lifeguard class costs $200, and the city refunds the $200 if you accept a job offer with the department.

who_can_apply: High school and middle school students. Tech theatre jobs are for ages 14 and up. For education jobs, you must go to every class. You must talk with the education director. You must do training at the start of the term. The age range for education jobs is not stated on the program page.
how_to_apply: New students fill out the Pre-Intern Program form. Then send the request form for the class you want. For tech theatre, call the volunteer coordinator at 563-292-8962. For education, call the education director at 515-974-5365.
notes: The request form on the page was labeled for the 2025-26 winter and spring season, so confirm it is current. The paid internships on the same page are for college students only.
duration: By semester (fall, winter, spring). Weekly hours are not stated on the program page.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer program

who_can_apply: Ages 14 and up. You must be 14 by June 1 to apply. You need to be comfortable outside in all weather.
how_to_apply: Fill out the volunteer form and one more set of questions. Then do an online training and orientation. Staff will contact you after they get your form. Send questions to heidi.anderson@polkcountyiowa.gov or call 515-323-5360.
notes: You keep track of your own hours and bring the paperwork for Silver Cord. The program page also lists Nature Center volunteering on the same volunteer menu.
duration: The full length of the camp you pick. Camps are 2 to 5 days, mostly in June and July, 9 AM to 3:30 PM at Jester Park.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role. Hours can count toward the Silver Cord award.

who_can_apply: Crew members are ages 14 to 18 in Polk County, Iowa. You must be able to work outside in all kinds of weather and get yourself to a daily meeting site.
how_to_apply: Watch the program page for the next application. For questions, email youthcorps@polkcountyiowa.gov.
notes: Summer 2026 sessions ran June 8 to 26 and July 13 to 31. The program provides transportation, a daily snack, lunch on Saturdays and all summer days, safety gear, and uniform shirts. Crew members are paid for days they show up to work.
duration: Summer: 3 weeks, Monday to Friday, 8 AM to 1:30 PM. Spring and fall sessions also run.
pay_detail: Stipend paid at the end of the session. The summer 2026 page said up to $1,100 for 3 weeks. The FAQ says at least $600. Crew members are paid for days they show up.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 12 to 18.
how_to_apply: Fill out the teen volunteer application and a waiver signed by a parent or guardian, in pen. Turn them in at your local Des Moines library. The volunteer leader will contact you. Summer volunteers must also go to a summer orientation session.
notes: The orientation event program page was from May 2025 and has already happened. Check with your branch for the next orientation date. The page does not name which branches take teens.
duration: No set hours on the page. Work happens during the school year and for the Summer Reading Program.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Teens earn volunteer hours.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 14 to 21.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application through the DMACC link on the program page. Keep your email and phone number current.
notes: The center is at 1171 7th Street, Des Moines, IA 50314 (email info@evelynkdaviscenter.org). The program page gives no phone number for Y-ExCL. Another page lists 515-697-7700 and a link on it shows 515-967-7700, so check before you call.
duration: 10 weeks: 2 weeks of training and 8 weeks of job placement
pay_detail: $12.00 an hour, 20 hours a week, Monday through Thursday

who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 18. No experience needed. Crews start and end in Eugene, OR or Boise, ID. You provide your own transportation to and from orientation.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply link on the Youth Camping page (Northwest Youth Corps application site). Contact info@nwyouthcorps.org.
notes: This is hard: you camp and work in all weather. If you leave before graduation you get a share of the stipend and lose the bonuses. The page lists possible high school credit. Oregon BOLI does not give work permits to minors ages 14 to 17. Employers need a certificate to hire minors.
duration: 4 to 5 weeks living outdoors (2026: June 13 to July 18; July 25 to Aug 29 or 30)
pay_detail: Up to $450 a week with bonuses, after $70 a week is deducted for food. $300 tuition fee, with need-based assistance.

who_can_apply: You must be 15 or older. You also need a current American Red Cross lifeguard certificate. The page links to upcoming classes.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply Now link on the lifeguard page, which goes to the district's job portal. Questions: isinkler@fargoparks.com (Aquatics team).
notes: Take the Red Cross certification class first. The page links to the class list. Fargo Park District also has other seasonal jobs and an internship program on its Employment page. North Dakota work rules for minors were not checked.
duration: Summer. Exact start and end dates are not stated on the program page.
pay_detail: $17 to $19 per hour

who_can_apply: Teens ages 12 to 18. A parent or guardian must sign the Teen Volunteer Permission Form.
how_to_apply: Register for each session at programregistration.library.fargond.gov or call 701.241.1495. Bring the signed permission form to your first session. The form is on the City of Fargo website.
notes: The page lists the month and day for each session but not the year. A good fit for a first volunteer experience; no commitment beyond a single session.
duration: One session of 2 hours (1 to 3 pm) on the first Saturday of each month, October to May.
pay_detail: Unpaid.

who_can_apply: Montana middle school and high school students (grades 6 to 12 in fall 2026 for the 2026 camp).
how_to_apply: Use the "Learn more & register for CSI camp" link on the MSU Continuing Education youth page.
notes: Held at the Gallatin College East Campus IT Cybersecurity Lab in Bozeman. Camp has no cost.
pay_detail: Free. Not a paid job.

who_can_apply: The First Seasons Community Center job has a minimum age of 15. The Warming House Attendant job has a minimum age of 16.
how_to_apply: Apply online at gfparks.org/employment/apply-online/. Questions: Grand Forks Park District Human Resources, (701) 746-2750, 1060 47th Ave S.
notes: Call to check these jobs are still open, because the Oct 1 date has passed. Other postings were not read, so their ages are unknown. These include skating instructor and indoor ice arena worker. Summer lifeguard jobs at Grand Forks outdoor pools are run by Choice Health & Fitness. Their current age rule is not confirmed.
duration: First Seasons: Saturdays 10 am to 5 pm, October to mid-April, flexible or split shifts, no evenings. Warming house: about 15 to 20 hours a week, weekdays 4 to 8 pm and weekends and holidays noon to 8 pm.
pay_detail: First Seasons Community Center: $14.00 an hour to start. Warming house attendant: $12.00 an hour to start.

who_can_apply: Applicants must be 16 or older for the Cleaning Squad. Most other fair jobs need 18 or more.
how_to_apply: Fill out the employment application on the fair careers page. It is online or in PDF. You can also pick one up at the State Fair Administrative Office, 501 E Fonner Park Rd, Suite 200, Grand Island, NE 68801. Or email it to the address on the flyer.
notes: Quote from the flyer: Applicants must be 16 years of age. The online application has a Social Security No. field and asks if you are authorized to work in the United States. Whether a Nebraska work permit is needed was not stated on the program pages.
duration: 2026 fair shifts: August 28 to September 7, 2026, plus training and orientation
pay_detail: Rate of pay starts at $15 per hour (2026 flyer).

who_can_apply: You must be 15 by the last day of the lifeguard course. You must pass a swim test: 300 yards, 2 minutes treading water, and a timed rescue.
how_to_apply: Look for openings and apply online at the City of Great Falls job site (governmentjobs.com/careers/greatfallsmt). The city phone number on its employment page is 406-771-1180. A Park and Recreation phone number is not stated.
notes: Classes need at least 5 people to run. The city offers certification classes through the year.
duration: Certification lasts 2 years
pay_detail: The city page says competitive wages and paid lifeguard certification. Hourly pay is not stated.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 15 to 18. You must sign up.
how_to_apply: Fill out the form on the program page. Or contact Graham Kerwin, Interim Education Manager. Call 406-727-8255. Or email graham@the-square.org.
notes: The program page shows a temporary hiatus in its April 2, 2026 update, until the museum finds an instructor. Call to ask if it has restarted.
duration: Weekly. The meeting time is not set yet on the program page.
pay_detail: Free to join. Food and art supplies are provided. No stipend is mentioned.

who_can_apply: Volunteers of any age can fill out the form. The form does not state a minimum age. If you are under 18, the form asks for a parent or guardian's contact information.
how_to_apply: Fill out the volunteer application form (a PDF on the library website) and give it to the library. The library is at 301 2nd Avenue North. Phone: 406-453-0349.
notes: The form asks for the last 4 digits of your Social Security number. It is for a background check and a workers compensation report. Ask the library about this before you fill it in. Call to ask about the current age rule and openings.
duration: Most roles need an ongoing time commitment (the form lists 1 month, 3 months, 6 months, ongoing or seasonal)
pay_detail: Volunteer role. No pay is mentioned.

who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 18 on June 1, 2026. Animal Care Assistants must be at least 14 and have done JZK the summer before. Advanced JZK is for returning 17 year olds.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. Then go to a 20 minute in-person interview. After you are accepted, pay the fee. Give a negative TB test by orientation. Then go to orientation.
notes: Teens arrange their own lunch and transportation. Contact: Education@GPZoo.org or (605) 367-7003. 2026 new teen interviews were April 11 and 12, so expect the 2027 cycle to start in winter or early spring.
duration: Whole summer; the 2026 session ran through August 9. At least two half-day shifts a week.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Teens pay a fee after they are accepted: $85 for zoo members, $100 for non-members. It covers materials and two uniform t-shirts. Scholarships may be available.

who_can_apply: High school students in Utah, Nevada, Montana, Idaho or Wyoming. You must be a rising sophomore or junior. You need consent from a parent or guardian.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply for Program button on the page when it opens.
notes: You must attend all 40 hours. A lab kit is mailed to your home. Contact: Monica Salas Jimenez, Monica.Salas@hci.utah.edu, 801-587-7885.
duration: Two weeks, Monday to Friday, 8:30 AM to 12:30 PM Mountain time (2026: July 6 to 17)
pay_detail: Up to $500

who_can_apply: High school students in Idaho, Montana, Nevada, Utah or Wyoming who finished at least freshman year. Rural students are very welcome. You need consent from a parent or guardian.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply for Program button on the page when it opens. Parent consent is required.
notes: It is online only. The program manager is Jill Christian. Her email is Jill.Christian@hci.utah.edu.
duration: Two weeks, Monday to Thursday, 8:30 AM to noon Mountain time (2026: July 13 to 16 and 20 to 23)
pay_detail: Up to $400

who_can_apply: Youth in grades 8 to 10 who are enrolled in 4-H and in the Know Your Government project this year. You can attend as a delegate two years.
how_to_apply: Join 4-H and the Know Your Government project, then register online when it opens in December. Questions: Mike Knutz, mknutz@uidaho.edu.
notes: The event page says grades 8 to 10. Ask your county 4-H office to confirm.
duration: Weekend (2027: February 13 to 15)
pay_detail: 2026 delegate fee was $230. Bus transportation to Boise is provided; steering committee members and chaperones can get up to $75 in help.

who_can_apply: Youth who have completed 8th through 12th grade. Both 4-H and non-4-H members can come. Adult chaperones must be certified.
how_to_apply: The program page does not say how to sign up. Email fourh@uidaho.edu or call 208-885-6321 to ask.
notes: Not stated on the program page: the exact location and a closing date. Plan to sign up by mid May, because prices go up on May 16. Teens do not have to be in 4-H.
duration: 4 days
pay_detail: 4-H members pay $335 if they sign up April 10 to May 15, or $395 May 16 to May 31. Non-4-H members pay $390 or $435. Price includes lodging, meals and transportation.

who_can_apply: Teens who are at least 14 by May 31 and no older than 17 during the program. First-time applicants need a letter of recommendation (not from a family member) and an interview.
how_to_apply: Submit the online application. If this is your first time, you also upload a letter of recommendation. Then you go to the zoo for an interview. If you have questions, email zooeducation@idahofallszoo.org.
notes: The 2026 sessions started June 9, June 30 and July 21. Fees cannot be refunded.
duration: 3-week sessions, three days a week, 9:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m.
pay_detail: Registration fee of $90 per 3-week session ($72 for Tautphaus Park Zoological Society members), nonrefundable. You get a uniform shirt and zoo admission during your session.

who_can_apply: Volunteers ages 8 and up. Volunteers 15 and younger must be with an adult volunteer. Each person makes their own account.
how_to_apply: Make an account and book a shift in the VolunteerHub system. Wear closed-toe, closed-heel shoes. Download the minor waiver if you are under 18.
notes: The warehouse is not heated or cooled, so wear layers. Groups of more than 18 use the group request form.
duration: Shifts are booked in advance (length not stated on the program page)
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteering.

who_can_apply: Ages 12 to 16. Teachers can also attend.
how_to_apply: Mail three things to the camp director at the University of Idaho in Moscow. Send a signed application, the health and medical release form, and the fee. If cost is a problem, ask about scholarships first.
notes: The camp is at the Central Idaho 4-H Camp north of Ketchum. Parents must drive campers to and from camp. The program page lists no closing date other than the May 20 payment date. Scholarship contact is Randy Brooks at 208-885-6356.
duration: 6 days (June 15 to 20 in 2026)
pay_detail: $310 for students. It covers food, lodging and medical insurance. Rides to camp are not included. Scholarships are offered through local Idaho Soil Conservation Districts.

who_can_apply: High school juniors. Other rules are not stated on the program page.
how_to_apply: Fill out the 2026-2027 ISAS application online. If you are not a junior yet, join the email list on the program page. Questions: isas@sde.idaho.gov.
notes: The program is competitive. Summer academy dates and cost are not stated on the program page. Program contact is Erin Lanigan at 208-885-1232.
duration: Online course during the school year. Summer academy is one week for chosen students.
pay_detail: Cost is not stated on the program page. Students may earn one science credit.

who_can_apply: The program is titled a high school internship. Age or grade rules are not stated on the program page.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. Selected students then have a group interview. It is at the Idaho State Museum. Questions? Email shseducation@ishs.idaho.gov. Or call (208) 334-2120.
notes: Pay and dates shown are from the 2025 to 2026 program details on the page; the 2026 to 2027 dates may differ. The page has an interest form for teen programs.
duration: The 2025 to 2026 run was November 4, 2025 to June 16, 2026, with Tuesday meetings from 4 to 7 p.m. and at least 3 volunteer shifts
pay_detail: $500 stipend paid in two parts (December and June), as listed for the 2025 to 2026 program.

who_can_apply: Your school has to offer the class. The program pages do not say which grades can join or how students are picked.
how_to_apply: Check the schools list on ijag.org to see if your school offers iJAG. Questions: (515) 216-3140 or info@ijag.org.
notes: iJAG is not a job or internship by itself. It is a class that connects students to employers. Whether your school has it depends on your district.
duration: A semester-based elective class.
pay_detail: No cost or pay is mentioned on the program pages.

who_can_apply: 11th or 12th graders who have taken a career and technical education (CTE) course. The fact sheet says students come from schools that have partnered with INL. Ask your school if it is a partner.
how_to_apply: Send a resume, an unofficial transcript and the application. INL checks that you are eligible, then interviews some applicants, then runs a background check. Ask your school CTE teacher or email russell.campbell@inl.gov.
notes: This card is based on the INL fact sheet dated January 2025. Confirm current dates at stem.inl.gov. Only students from partner schools can apply.
duration: 6 weeks, mid June to early August
pay_detail: Paid. The pay rate is not stated on the fact sheet. Transportation, food and safety gear are provided.

who_can_apply: Iowa only. Iowa 4-H members ages 16 to 20 on January 1 of the year they apply. They must have at least four years in a county 4-H program.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. The link is on the program page. The page does not list the parts of the application. Ambassadors go to monthly meetings and retreats. They find their own rides, meet with a career mentor and finish 10 hours of community or fair service.
notes: The page lists no fee or pay. Ambassadors must find their own rides. Contacts: Amy Powell, ampowell@iastate.edu, or Celine Beggs-Shoemaker, cmbeggs@iastate.edu. The site has no Iowa region, so this card is tagged national and teens in other states may still see it under National. The Iowa only line at the start of What you do and Who can apply is the only guard.
duration: One program year, August to the next August
pay_detail: The page lists no fee or pay.

who_can_apply: Iowa only. Iowa youth in grades 7 to 12.
how_to_apply: The page does not describe how to apply. Contact Iowa 4-H: 515-294-1017 or iowa4hmail@iastate.edu. Financial aid links are on the page.
notes: Cost is not stated. The page links to Iowa 4-H Foundation financial aid. Confirm dates with your county 4-H office first. The site has no Iowa region, so this card is tagged national and teens in other states may still see it under National. The Iowa only line at the start of What you do and Who can apply is the only guard.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Cost is not stated. The page links to Iowa 4-H Foundation financial aid.

who_can_apply: Iowa only. Iowa 4-H members in grades 9 to 12. Up to 16 are picked. The page says members who hold a Reporter, Historian or Photographer role, or like media projects, fit best.
how_to_apply: Apply through State 4-H Recognition Day in 4-H Online: a one-page cover letter and a one-page resume. No interview, selection is from the written materials. You can apply more than once.
notes: The page does not say whether it pays or costs anything. Contact on the page: Clark Colby, 515-419-3301. The site has no Iowa region, so this card is tagged national and teens in other states may still see it under National. The Iowa only line at the start of What you do and Who can apply is the only guard.
duration: Events run June to August
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Iowa only. Iowa 4-H members in grade 10 or 11 at the time of application. You may apply a second year.
how_to_apply: Sign up in 4-H Online. Then apply at State 4-H Recognition Day with a one-page cover letter and a one-page resume. Strong applications get an interview.
notes: The page does not say whether there is a cost. Contact: st4hcounciladvisors@iastate.edu, 515-294-1017. The site has no Iowa region, so this card is tagged national and teens in other states may still see it under National. The Iowa only line at the start of What you do and Who can apply is the only guard.
duration: June of one year through July of the next
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Iowa only. Volunteer spots are open to Iowa 4-H youth who fill out the form. Paid youth staff spots are for 4-H members or alumni. Age rules are not stated on the page.
how_to_apply: Volunteers and youth staff each use an online form listed on the page. For 2027 interns, watch the page in December 2026. Email statefair4h@iastate.edu.
notes: Volunteers in the Exhibits Building or Livestock can ask for Youth Inn lodging. The Iowa State Fair also lists about 1,600 seasonal jobs on its own job site. That page does not state a minimum age or pay. The site has no Iowa region, so this card is tagged national and teens in other states may still see it under National. The Iowa only line at the start of What you do and Who can apply is the only guard.
duration: Iowa State Fair, Aug 10 to 23, 2026
pay_detail: Youth staff and intern jobs are paid. Pay rates are not stated. Volunteer spots are unpaid.

who_can_apply: Iowa only. Iowa youth in grades 4 to 12 (Clover Kids is K to 3).
how_to_apply: Start on the Join 4-H page, or call 515-294-1017 or email iowa4hmail@iastate.edu. Your county Extension office can place you in a club.
notes: Cost is not stated on the page. The site has no Iowa region, so this card is tagged national and teens in other states may still see it under National. The Iowa only line at the start of What you do and Who can apply is the only guard.
duration: Ongoing
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Iowa residents who have finished 11th grade and have at least one semester left before graduating. Must be a U.S. citizen or lawful permanent resident. Exchange students are not accepted. This program is for boys. A local American Legion Post must pick and sponsor you.
how_to_apply: Contact your local American Legion Post and ask to be picked as a delegate. In January you get a selection email from your post. It has the information you need to register online. The Boys State site also has an Interest Form.
notes: The program does not provide rides. Delegates who bring cars cannot use them during the program, except in emergencies. A valid state ID card is needed to enter Camp Dodge. The program page says the Graduating Class of 2028 is the group for 2027.
duration: 6 days (June 20 to 25, 2027)
pay_detail: Unpaid, but free to attend. The local American Legion Post or other donors pay the fee.

who_can_apply: Any high school student in Iowa or Nebraska who is a U.S. citizen or lawful permanent resident. Your paper must follow the rules in the Iowa Research Handbook. Schools can also bring up to five students to attend without presenting.
how_to_apply: Do a research project and write a paper that follows the Iowa Research Handbook. Submit the paper on the program site by the due date. Accepted papers present at the symposium.
notes: You need a research project first. The national symposium is April 20 to 24, 2027.
duration: Two-day symposium on February 22 and 23, 2027
pay_detail: Free to enter and attend. Top finalists can win scholarship prizes.

who_can_apply: Students who are in 10th, 11th or 12th grade when they apply. Students from outside the United States may apply. Students in 9th grade can no longer apply.
how_to_apply: Apply online on Submittable during the two-week window. Send a writing sample of up to ten pages. Also send a statement of purpose of 1 to 2 pages. Ask an English or writing teacher, tutor or mentor to upload one letter of recommendation. Decisions go out by email on April 9, 2027.
notes: Costs money. The program also runs 6-week online courses in winter and summer. See the program site for those. Questions: iyws@uiowa.edu or 319-335-4209.
duration: 2 weeks
pay_detail: $2,500 for one 2-week session in 2027 (room, board and teaching included). There is a $10 reading fee to apply, and it can be waived. Need-based financial aid is offered.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 10 and 11. The page describes it as a program for advanced high school students.
how_to_apply: Apply online. Fill in your information and pay the $95 fee. Get two letters from non-relative adults (one academic, one character). Write two essays of up to 750 words. Upload your transcript and SAT or ACT scores. Questions: summer@belinblank.org.
notes: Confirm the 2027 cost with summer@belinblank.org: the page shows the $7,500 fee for the 2026 session and does not show a 2027 fee.
duration: 5.5 weeks, June 16 to July 23, 2027
pay_detail: The 2026 session fee was $7,500 (room, board, materials, activities and 3 credit hours). The 2027 fee is not confirmed on the page; the page says to check with summer@belinblank.org. Travel and personal costs are extra. Financial aid may cover up to 95 percent. There is a $95 application fee that is not refunded.

who_can_apply: Iowa only. Students in schools with a local FFA chapter. The page does not state grades or ages.
how_to_apply: Find your school's chapter with the Chapter Locator on iowaffa.com, or ask your ag teacher. Dues are not stated on the page.
notes: About 20,800 members in 273 chapters (per the page). Only schools with an ag program have a chapter. The site has no Iowa region, so this card is tagged national and teens in other states may still see it under National. The Iowa only line at the start of What you do and Who can apply is the only guard.
duration: School year
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Students with a disability who are 14 to 21 years old. Talk to your school staff or your Vocational Rehabilitation high school contact to sign up.
how_to_apply: Talk with your school staff or your Vocational Rehabilitation high school contact. You can also apply online, with a paper form, or at your local office. Call 1-800-532-1486 with questions.
notes: The program page links to the Transition Alliance Program (TAP). It does not describe TAP. Work-based learning is one part of Pre-ETS. The program page does not say if the work is paid.
duration: Not stated on the program page
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page

who_can_apply: Ages 14 through 24 who face barriers to employment. Meeting the rules does not guarantee a spot. Funds are limited and staff pick youth who are 'most in need' and likely to succeed.
how_to_apply: Contact a youth case manager at the nearest Job Service North Dakota office. Fargo: 1350 32nd St S, 701-239-7300, infojsfg@nd.gov. Bismarck: 1601 E Century Ave, 701-328-5000, infojsbis@nd.gov. Grand Forks: 1501 28th Ave S, 701-795-3700, infojsgf@nd.gov.
notes: Not for every teen. The handbook says the program is not an entitlement. The exact list of barriers and income rules was not in the program pages, so ask the case manager. The handbook is dated 10.21 in its file name, so confirm details by phone. North Dakota work rules for minors were not checked.
duration: Work experience can happen any time of year. Length is not stated.
pay_detail: Work experience pays at least minimum wage, paid through Job Service. Pay covers up to 25 hours per week.

who_can_apply: Most volunteer positions take youth 14 and older. Summer teen volunteer jobs are open to ages 13 and older as of June 1. Each job posting lists its own minimum age.
how_to_apply: Register in the library's volunteer database. This is a Samaritan volunteer profile. Then sign up for an opening with the Sign Up button. If no shift is listed, the Volunteer Coordinator follows up with you.
notes: Quote from the page: We welcome and encourage youth volunteers 14 years and older for most volunteer positions. The page says over 900 teens through adults volunteer each year. You can also become a Swift Volunteer for last-minute needs, with no obligation.
duration: One-time, short-term or weekly shifts
pay_detail: Unpaid. The library records and verifies service hours weekly for schools.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 13 to 18 as of January 1 of the event year.
how_to_apply: Registration for 2026 is closed. The page tells youth to let their Extension unit know which class session they choose. The page does not say how to register next year. Email kansas4h@ksu.edu with questions.
notes: Not stated on the program page: whether you must be a 4-H member. Ask your county Extension office.
duration: About 3 days (June 3 to 5 in 2026)

who_can_apply: Students going into 9th grade can join the rising freshman program. Students going into 10th, 11th or 12th grade can join the other program. The page does not list an age rule.
how_to_apply: Use the application link for your program on the program page. You must go to an in-person orientation. Email VolunteerApplications@KUMC.edu or call 913-588-6560.
notes: 2026 sessions ran June 1 to July 30. There is also a program page for the Olathe location.
duration: Rising sophomore to senior: one 2-week session, Monday to Thursday. Rising freshman: half days on Friday mornings, at least 6 Fridays.
pay_detail: Volunteer program.

who_can_apply: LIT is for ages 14 to 16. CIT is for ages 16 to 17. The page says CIT is especially for rising 12th graders.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Letter of Interest for LIT or CIT on the program page. You then get instructions on how to register. Call 785-257-3221 with questions.
notes: A camper scholarship (campership) form is linked on the page. Check the page in early 2027 for new dates and prices.
duration: Five nights
pay_detail: 2026 cost for five nights: LIT $800, $700 or $600 by tier. CIT $650, $550 or $450 by tier. The page says the program can be attended at no cost through a donation to the Kansas 4-H Foundation.

who_can_apply: Students entering 11th or 12th grade who are interested in a health care career. Limited to 25 students.
how_to_apply: Register online when registration opens on January 4, 2027. Use the link on the Health Science Explorers page. Contact the coordinator listed on the page with questions.
notes: The same page lists a virtual Career Club for grades 9 to 12. It meets on the second Wednesday each month, 7 to 8 pm. It also lists a yearly Health Careers Fair at the Crowne Plaza in Kearney.
duration: September to May, first Wednesday of each month, 8:30 a.m. to 3 p.m.
pay_detail: $100 for the program, with financial help available. Lunch is provided. Students who finish earn a $1,000 UNK scholarship.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 17. Volunteers commit to a minimum of six months and 100 service hours, about four hours of service each week.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Teen Volunteer Program application on the Kootenai Health volunteer page. Then wait to hear from them if there is an opening. Phone (208) 625-4645 or email volunteerservices@kh.org.
notes: The page says volunteer roles do not include internships or clinical shadowing. Volunteer office hours are Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 4 p.m.
duration: At least 6 months and 100 service hours
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer work.

who_can_apply: Volunteers must be at least 12 years old. Volunteers under 18 need a parent or guardian to sign the application.
how_to_apply: Complete the online volunteer application. After you apply, the Volunteer Coordinator contacts you. This takes a couple of weeks. They set up your orientation. Email volcoor@lclsonline.org. Or call 307.773.7225.
notes: The library also has a Teen Zone page. A background check is required for volunteers age 18 and older.
duration: Not stated on the program page
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer work.

who_can_apply: Students entering their sophomore, junior or senior year of high school who are interested in architecture or design. Priority goes to students with financial need. It also goes to students from select Kansas City and St. Louis area school districts.
how_to_apply: Register online. Fee waiver applications have two short answer questions. They ask why you want to attend and what your extracurricular activities are. Ask for a fee waiver on the application if you need one.
notes: There are optional bus rides to and from Lawrence. Fee waiver recipients from Kansas City get them.
duration: One week. 2026 dates were May 31 to June 6, 2026.
pay_detail: $1,000 (housing, meals, studio fees, materials and evening activities), with a $150 deposit at registration. Fee waivers are available for a select number of students with financial need.

who_can_apply: Rising 9th and 10th graders go to the July 11 to 16, 2027 camp. Rising 11th and 12th graders go to the July 18 to 23, 2027 camp. Everyone stays overnight in the residence hall, even if they live nearby.
how_to_apply: Register online when registration opens in February. Send questions to the camp email. It is on the page.
notes: The page says all students must stay overnight. Check the page for cost and the theme once posted.
duration: One week each (two camps in July 2027)
pay_detail: Cost not stated on the program page

who_can_apply: Students in grades 7 to 12. Adults 18 and over use a different application. The library says it does not offer community service hours at this time.
how_to_apply: Fill out the VolunTeen application when it opens. Then go to a one-hour new volunteer orientation, a 15-minute interview, and a 1.5-hour training shift with a mentor. Questions go to the Teen Librarian at the email on the page.
notes: Quote from the page: we do not offer community service opportunities at this time. So this is not for court or school-required hours. There is also a VolunTeen Youth Program Assistant (Summer) position.
duration: One-hour shift each week, evenings and weekends, for a semester (option to extend)
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Students entering grades 7 to 12 in fall 2027. Past members are not guaranteed a spot back.
how_to_apply: Apply when the window opens, choosing the Animal Care track or the Education track. Questions go to the Education Team at the number on the page.
notes: The page lists a $250 per session fee. Education track volunteers work with the summer camp program.
duration: Session dates for 2027 not stated on the program page
pay_detail: Volunteer program. Any cost is not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Anyone who has finished 5th grade and is under 19 (teen track). You also need approval from the City of Lincoln Human Resources Department.
how_to_apply: Download and print the Minor Volunteer Application (under age 19). Fill it out. Then contact the Volunteer Coordinator at the library branch you want. Expect a 1 to 2 week wait before you hear back.
notes: Library address: 136 South 14th Street, Lincoln, NE 68508. Phone 402-441-8500. Branches may not be taking new volunteers, so call first. Tasks also listed for National Honor Society and Government and Politics students needing 10 hours.
duration: Teen Advisory Board: one meeting a month, August to May. VolunTEEN: 1 to 2 times a week during Summer Reading Challenge (May, June, July). School groups: 10 hours or more in a semester.

who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 24. You must meet WIOA income and barrier rules and enroll in the YESS Program before you are placed.
how_to_apply: Apply to the City of Lincoln job posting for the program. Staff at the American Job Center then contact you to check if you qualify. After you enroll, you are matched with a City department. Call 402-441-7975 with questions.
notes: The page does not mention work permits. Weekly workshops and possible tuition help are listed.
duration: June 4 to July 29 in 2026
pay_detail: $16 per hour plus a $200 bonus for finishing. Up to 30 hours a week. You also get a free Chromebook.

who_can_apply: Students going into grades 9 to 12. The page text still says the 2026-27 school year, so check the grade rule for 2027 camps. This is not a commuter camp.
how_to_apply: Pre-register by the January deadline. This helps you get priority scholarships. Then register online when registration opens in February. Space is limited. It is first come, first served, with a waitlist.
notes: Camper limits are small (15 to 20 per camp for the camps listed). The page lists the years only as 2027 in the heading, so confirm the Dec 18 and Jan 22 dates are for the 2026-27 cycle. Contact: the Big Red Camps email on the page.
duration: One week: June 6 to June 11, 2027
pay_detail: Tuition for the camps listed: $625 to $850 for the week (early, regular and late rates vary by camp). Housing and food are included. Scholarships are offered.

who_can_apply: Lincoln-area high school students who are 16 by June 1 and have not graduated. U.S. citizenship is required. May 2025 graduates are eligible if they attend UNL in fall 2026.
how_to_apply: Fill out the application on the program page. Ask one teacher to send a reference by the deadline. Students who apply to several summer research programs can only do this one if picked.
notes: Work days are Monday to Friday between 8 a.m. and 5 p.m. The page does not mention work permits.
duration: About 8 weeks, starting June 2 in 2026
pay_detail: $15 per hour, 20 hours a week (2026)

who_can_apply: High school students interested in computing. The page does not list grades or ages. The page says the camp is designed for students with little to no computing experience. Students planning to start college in fall 2027 get priority based on total applications.
how_to_apply: Send a short essay, your coding level, your school grades and a school transcript. You can add a scholarship request. The page points to an Apply Online page on the Raikes site.
notes: Students who expect to start college in fall 2028 are considered if they finished pre-calculus before camp. Contact is 402-472-9097.

pay_detail: $3,000 in 2026. Nebraska high school students get $1,000 off, so $2,000. The fee covers housing, meals, teaching and activities. Full and partial scholarships are offered.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 9 to 12 who like livestock and related careers. Students from across the country can apply.

notes: Only 20 students are accepted. You stay in campus housing with program staff.
duration: 4 days (June 10 to 13 in 2026)
pay_detail: $50 fee to hold your spot, due only if you are accepted. A livestock industry group pays for the other costs. You pay your own travel.

who_can_apply: Students going into their sophomore, junior or senior year of high school.

notes: Each extra brunch guest costs $15. Check the page in spring 2027 for new dates.
duration: 5 days (June 9 to 13 in 2026)
pay_detail: $75 per student in 2026. It covers 4 nights in a K-State residence hall, all meals and a Saturday brunch for up to two guests.

who_can_apply: High school juniors and seniors interested in health care careers. Small groups of 20 students per session.
how_to_apply: Join the 2027 Interest List on the program page. The college says details are added as they become available. Questions: College of Health and Human Sciences, phone number on the page.
notes: Quote from the page: Join our 2027 Interest List. The page does not show application dates yet.
duration: One week, June 2027 (two sessions planned). In 2026 the sessions were June 7 to 12 and June 21 to 26.
pay_detail: 2027 cost: not yet posted. The page does not state the 2026 cost.

who_can_apply: High school students. The page does not list a grade or age rule.

notes: The page calls it a three-day program but lists June 24 to 27. Check the dates when 2027 registration opens.
duration: June 24 to 27 in 2026
pay_detail: $800 in 2026. A limited number of scholarships are offered for students with financial need. Kansas and Kansas City area students get priority.

who_can_apply: High school students in grades 9 to 12. The page lists 12 spots.

duration: June 7 to 10, 2027
pay_detail: Cost not yet posted

who_can_apply: The high school day is for students entering grades 9 to 12, and college students. Other days are for younger grades.
how_to_apply: Registration for 2026 is closed. The program page does not say how next year signs up. Check it again in spring 2027.

duration: 1 day for the high school group (Monday, July 27 in 2026). Other grade groups came July 28 and 29.
pay_detail: $125 per camper in 2026. Lunch and snacks are provided.

who_can_apply: Teens at least 16 years old. You must be in school in good standing or working toward a GED. A parent or guardian must agree.

You also need proof of immunizations, references and an interview. Contact Anne Owens at anne.owens@mercyone.org. Or call 515-358-9265.
notes: Are you 14 or 15? Look at the teen program at UnityPoint Iowa Lutheran Hospital.

who_can_apply: Volunteers must be 12 or older. Anyone under 18 needs permission from a parent or legal guardian. An older library event page lists the teen program as ages 12 to 18, grades 7 to 12.

duration: Not stated on the program page
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role

who_can_apply: Enrolled high school students (per the summer program page). The Fall 2026 event page does not list ages.
how_to_apply: Subscribe to the museum newsletter to hear when enrollment opens. For the Fall 2026 project use the Register button on its event page. Museum phone: 406-728-0447.
notes: It is not clear if the Fall 2026 project is part of the same program as Summer TAP. Ask the museum.
duration: Summer program. Fall 2026 project: 8 weeks, Thursdays 2:30 to 5 PM, Oct 1 to Nov 19, 2026
pay_detail: Cost and stipend are not stated on the program pages.

who_can_apply: The page says it accepts volunteers of all ages and abilities. It does not list a teen rule.

notes: Call to confirm the minimum age for the role you want. The page does not state one.
duration: Varies by role
pay_detail: Volunteer roles. No pay is mentioned.

notes: The page said summer jobs were "posted soon", so check the portal for current openings.
duration: Not stated on the program page
pay_detail: The city reimburses the Red Cross training course if you accept a lifeguard or Water Safety Instructor job. Hourly pay is not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Teens in grades 7 to 12.
how_to_apply: Email children@missoulapubliclibrary.org. Ask for more info. Ask to join the email list. Main library phone: 406-721-2665.
notes: Snacks are free at every meeting. The page does not say how many volunteer hours you can earn.
duration: Meets Thursdays, 3:30 to 5:30 PM, in the Art Box on level two
pay_detail: Members earn volunteer hours. No pay is stated.

who_can_apply: Any Montana high school student in any grade who likes history, law and government. Students from outside Missoula can apply. They must plan their own travel and place to stay.
how_to_apply: Not offered in 2026. Fill out the interest form on the program page to get news. Contacts: Professor Claire Arcenas or Professor Jody Pavilack. They work at the University of Montana.
notes: Based on the 2025 page. The topic may change in 2027.
duration: One week, 9 AM to 4 PM (2025: July 21-25)
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Students ages 13 to 19 who go to Big Sky, Browning, Heart Butte, Hellgate or Sentinel High School. You must be a likely first-generation college student or from a family that meets the income rules. The page describes the program for college-bound students with a GPA of at least 2.5. You must be a U.S. citizen, national or permanent resident.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply page for the program on the University of Montana site. Call the TRIO Upward Bound office at 406-243-2219. Or use the email on the page: jonathan.carter@umontana.edu.
notes: Check the dates with the office. Page dates and title do not match.
duration: Six weeks
pay_detail: Free. No stipend is mentioned on the program page.

who_can_apply: Montana 4-H youth who are at least 13 years old as of October 1 of the 4-H year. Chaperones must be certified 4-H volunteers or MSU Extension staff, age 21 or older.
how_to_apply: Register online in the 4-H Zsuite system. Each county has its own deadlines and steps, so call your county Extension office early.
notes: You do not have to enter a contest. Youth State Awards are due May 1.
duration: 4 days (July 14 to 17, 2027)
pay_detail: $285. It covers lodging for 3 nights, 7 meals, program costs and a t-shirt. Campus parking costs extra.

who_can_apply: Must be 14 by October 1 of the current year, enrolled in 4-H for at least 2 years and this year, and be or have been a Junior Leader or club officer. A maximum age is not stated on the program page.
how_to_apply: County level: fill out an application. Then interview with the County Council. State officer: send the application to the Montana 4-H Center. It must be postmarked by June 15.
notes: You must already be in 4-H. The state team page lists five state officer jobs (for example President and Publicity Chair). Contact your county extension office. The state officer page does not state the term length for officers.
duration: Not stated on the program page
pay_detail: Unpaid leadership role. Cost not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Montana 4-H youth who are at least 14 years old as of October 1 of the 4-H year. Counties send ambassadors and teen leaders. Chaperones must be certified 4-H volunteers or MSU Extension staff, age 21 or older.
how_to_apply: Register online in the 4-H Zsuite system. Call your county MSU Extension office for county rules. Fill in your info and waivers before the event.
notes: Cancel before sign-up closes for a full refund. Dress is business casual on Saturday. Dress for the banquet is business professional to semi-formal.
duration: Weekend (November 6 to 8, 2026)
pay_detail: $195. It covers lodging (2 to 4 people per room), Saturday and Sunday meals and program costs. Friday dinner is on your own.

who_can_apply: Ages 15 to 18. You must be a 4-H member in your home county for at least three consecutive years. You need your county agent's approval.
how_to_apply: Fill out the application and send it. Email is preferred. You can also text 406-624-9835, fax 406-994-5417 or mail it to Montana 4-H Foundation, Inc., PO Box 173580, Bozeman.
notes: The page lists two at-large youth seats. Ask your county agent early because their approval is required.
duration: Two-year term (the page says it will change to one year)
pay_detail: Unpaid board seat. Cost not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Montana teens ages 14 to 18. You must live in Montana. Teens from other states will not be considered.
how_to_apply: Online application filled out by the teen and a parent or guardian. The parent or guardian must sign a Youth Program Release form that is emailed after you submit. Email youthprograms@mtcorps.org with questions.
notes: Yellowstone sessions leave from Bozeman and Glacier sessions leave from Kalispell. Next dates not posted yet.
duration: 9-day sessions
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer crew. $100 service award and up to 64 service hours on successful completion. The program is free to join.

who_can_apply: Montana teens ages 17 to 18. Montana residency is required. You must commit to the full summer.
how_to_apply: Online application. A parent or guardian must sign the Youth Program Release that is emailed after you submit. Interview, then a decision within 2 weeks. Email youthprograms@mtcorps.org with questions.
notes: 2026 crews were in Helena, Kalispell (Flathead Youth Corps) and Missoula. Participants must commit to the full summer. Next dates not posted yet.
duration: About 8 weeks (2026 crews: mid June to early August)
pay_detail: Living allowance of $1,200 every two weeks before taxes, plus an AmeriCorps education award ($1,565.08 for the 2026 crews).

who_can_apply: Montana high school students who are rising juniors or seniors and want a career in science or engineering. No GPA or age rule is listed.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application when it opens. Questions: metcamp@mtech.edu.
notes: The dates and deadline come from the 2026 news release on the Montana Tech site. The program page says Montana high school students are invited to apply. Watch for a new release around February 2027.
duration: 1 week (June 21 to 26 in 2026)
pay_detail: Free. Lodging, meals and course materials are provided. You must arrange your own ride to campus.

who_can_apply: Teens must be 16 to 18 years of age before graduating high school. A parent must sign a consent form.
how_to_apply: Submit the online VolunTEEN application. Also send in the VolunTEEN Program Guidelines and the Parental Consent Form. Then you do a job shadow. After that, you go to an orientation and an interview. You also do onboarding and health steps.
notes: Adults 18 and older use a different program with 30 hours in three months. The page says the wait from application to first shift is about six weeks for adults. Sturgis, Custer, Lead-Deadwood and Spearfish hospitals have their own volunteer contacts; the page does not say they take teens.
duration: One 2 to 4 hour shift a week, same day and time, for 10 to 12 weeks (at least 30 hours).
pay_detail: Unpaid.

who_can_apply: Volunteers must be 13 or older. If you are under 18, a parent or guardian must sign a consent form. Library staff will talk with you. They may ask for personal references.
how_to_apply: Email the Volunteer Coordinator at tolmanj@cityofnampa.us. You can find it on the volunteer page. Or call the library at 208-468-5800. Ask when applications open again.
notes: The site also lists a Teen Advisory Council under its Support section. The volunteer page does not explain how to join it.
duration: Schedule set one-on-one with the library manager
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role

who_can_apply: You must be 16 years old and a 10th or 11th grader in the year you apply. You must live in Nebraska. You must be a US citizen or have proof of work authorization. Commuter only, no housing.
how_to_apply: Apply during the early spring window on the program page. You need teacher recommendations. Spots are very limited.
notes: Research areas include biology and physics. They include chemistry too. The featured project has a lab. It is at the University of Nebraska-Lincoln.
duration: Up to 8 weeks, early June to early August
pay_detail: $15 per hour for 20 to 40 hours a week, up to 8 weeks. Pay and schedule are set by the faculty mentor.

who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 22. The program page does not say if you must be a 4-H member.
how_to_apply: Get the form from Ambassador Resources on the NDSU 4-H leadership page. Send it to the ND 4-H Center for Youth Development.
notes: Selection is the Saturday before Thanksgiving at 4-H Camp in Washburn. Questions: ndsu.4hambassadors@ndsu.edu.
duration: Not stated on the program page.
pay_detail: Cost not listed on the program page.

who_can_apply: Youth who have finished seventh grade. You do not need to be in 4-H.
how_to_apply: Use the registration link on the NDSU event page.
notes: Ask North Dakota 4-H about financial help. The page does not mention scholarships.
duration: 4 days. The 2026 conference was June 22 to 25 at NDSU in Fargo.
pay_detail: Teens pay. Early-bird price was $365 per person (Thanksgiving through December), then the price rises $10 a month. Payment is due June 1.

who_can_apply: Grades 7 to 12. The program page does not say whether you must be in 4-H.
how_to_apply: Use the registration link on the NDSU event page.
notes: Cost is not listed yet. Call North Dakota 4-H or your county Extension office to ask.
duration: Weekend, Feb 14 to 15, 2027. If weather cancels it, make-up dates are April 4 to 5, 2027.
pay_detail: Cost not listed on the program page.

who_can_apply: Current 10th or 11th graders who live in North Dakota. You can attend a public or non-public school. You need a cumulative GPA of 3.25 or higher. Selection uses a personal essay of 250 words or less. It also uses two recommendations (one teacher, one counselor or administrator) and a transcript.
how_to_apply: Apply online on the NDSU Governor's School site (2026 cycle). You need a personal essay of 250 words or less. You also need one teacher recommendation. You need one counselor or administrator recommendation too. Questions? Email ndsu.otl@ndsu.edu.
notes: The NDSU page says the program runs every other summer. The next session's host, dates and portal are not posted on the program pages. Ask NDSU at ndsu.otl@ndsu.edu.
duration: Four weeks. 2026 dates were June 8 to July 2.
pay_detail: The NDSU pages do not list a cost. A UND article says a North Dakota Department of Public Instruction grant covered tuition and on-campus housing for the 2025 session. Check that this still holds.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 24. Income and home address rules are not stated on the program page.
how_to_apply: Applications are not open yet. Check the Oak Futures page in spring 2027.
notes: The program page does not say where you must live. Ask before you apply.
duration: Nine weeks for the summer option; a year-round option also exists. Exact dates not stated.
pay_detail: Paid, part-time, 20 to 30 hours per week. Pay rate not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 15 to 19 pick the Teen Connection type on the application. The page does not list a city or school rule.
