notes: The application form asks for a Social Security number, a date of birth and an emergency contact. The same page also lists KIDS Nebraska. It is for young people ages 13 to 18 in Nebraska and western Iowa. No prior medical experience is needed.
duration: Not stated on the program page
pay_detail: Unpaid. The application says services are donated and there is no payment.

who_can_apply: Current juniors at Omaha North, Omaha Central or Omaha South high school. You must be 16 or older by the start of the program. There are no exceptions. You need your own place to stay and a ride each day. You must go to every activity.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online form. A STEM teacher and a school counselor must also send in a review by the deadline.
notes: Only three Omaha high schools can apply. The poster session is typically held in early August. Start and end dates are Not stated on the program page.
duration: 8 weeks
pay_detail: Students can earn up to $4,800 for the hours they work.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 5 to 18. Age is counted on January 1 of the 4-H year. You must be 8 by then for competitive events, large animal, shooting sports or food preservation projects.
how_to_apply: Join an existing club or start a new one. Then enroll online in 4HOnline. Call 402-444-7804 if you need help finding a club.
notes: A new club needs one trained 4-H volunteer and five youth from three different families. The page says enrollment in 4HOnline begins October 17. Clubs must meet at least six times per year.
duration: The 4-H year runs Oct 1 to Sep 30.
pay_detail: Enrollment fee is $10 per youth per year.

who_can_apply: Age 16 or older, unless an adult comes with you. Some jobs need you to be 18.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Volunteer Interest Form. Then you finish an application, an interview and training. This includes a background check.
notes: Quote from the page: Must be 16 years of age, unless accompanied by an adult. Check which roles are open to teens under 18.
duration: You must meet a minimum number of hours each year (the number is not stated on the program page)
pay_detail: Unpaid. Perks include a 25 percent museum shop discount and a 25 percent soda fountain discount on days you volunteer.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 7 and 8.
how_to_apply: Come back to the page on January 5, 2027 for application details.
notes: The 2026 Jr Crew program has concluded. Zoo Crew is for grades 9 to 12.
duration: Summer season. Exact length not stated on the program page.
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page

who_can_apply: High school students who love art and are committed to their education. Priority goes to students from schools not yet in the program.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application on the program page. Staff interview applicants (mostly in March).
notes: Core program meets at Kent Bellows Studio, 3303 Leavenworth Street. Foundations meets at the Joslyn. The page also lists a Teen Pop-Up Market hosted by teens and an open call for youth ages 13 to 19.
duration: Twice a week: 4 to 6 pm in the school year, 3 to 6 pm in summer
pay_detail: Pay-as-you-are-able tuition of $1 to $600 per trimester. Supplies are provided.

who_can_apply: Incoming and current high school students in the Omaha metro area. You must commit to at least 1 year of service.
how_to_apply: Print the Volunteen form from the page and fill it out. Send it to the Volunteer Office.
notes: Minimum age is not stated on the program page. The free meal on the page is listed under VIP perks. The page does not say it applies to Volunteens. Methodist Hospital and Methodist Women's Hospital may both have waiting lists.
duration: At least 1 year
pay_detail: Unpaid. Volunteers get a free cafeteria meal on the day they volunteer.

who_can_apply: Anyone 16 or older who can commit to six months and 2 to 4 hours a week and finish orientation.
how_to_apply: Submit the online volunteer application. Volunteer Services reviews it. They call you for a welcome meeting. You talk about what you like and when you can come. Then finish New Volunteer Orientation and onboarding.
notes: Quote from the page: Be at least 16 years old.
duration: Initial six-month commitment, 2 to 4 hours a week
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Anyone age 11 or older. Youth ages 11 to 18 need a parent or legal guardian to approve. The page does not list a city or school rule.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online volunteer form. There is one form for Central Library and another for all other branches. Youth and summer reading volunteers need a parent or guardian signature before starting.
notes: The library says it may not be able to place each applicant. It has the right to reject any application without reason. It reserves the right to do a background check or check references. Quote from the volunteer policy: OPL accepts volunteers ages 11 and older. The Central Library has its own volunteer form. It is linked on the volunteer page.
duration: Short-term or ongoing, depending on the task
pay_detail: Unpaid. The library says it can provide volunteer hours for court-related community service.

who_can_apply: Omaha Public Schools sophomores, juniors and seniors who are on track to graduate. CNA students must be 16 by May of that year. EMT students must be seniors.
how_to_apply: Apply with your 6-digit student ID. The application is shared by QR code and email. Have your GPA, counselor name and email, top 2 pathways, and a list of activities and volunteer work ready.
notes: Only for OPS students. The page says the district provides bus transportation. The Career Center is at 3230 Burt Street, Omaha.
duration: Not stated on the program page.
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Youth and young adults ages 14 to 21. The program page does not list city or school rules.
how_to_apply: Apply online at StepUpOmaha.com. The news release says to apply there.
notes: This card uses the March 2026 news release on the organizer's site. Check StepUpOmaha.com for 2027 dates. The release says roughly 100 employers took part in 2025.
duration: 2026 program ran June 2 through July 31
pay_detail: Interns can earn $1,800 to $3,000 or more during the summer (2026 news release).

who_can_apply: Juniors and seniors who are at least 16 at the start of the school year. Your school district must take part (districts around Omaha). You need grades of B or above in Algebra 1, Biology, a physical science and a third year of science. You also need parent permission and an interview.
how_to_apply: Check that you meet the criteria and that your school district takes part. Review the forms. Then apply online. Eligible students are scheduled for an interview. Then they are notified by email.
notes: The page says there are only 65 spots a year. Just one-third of applicants are accepted. Participating public school districts include Omaha, Millard, Bellevue, Elkhorn and Westside. They also include Council Bluffs Community Schools, Gretna, Bennington, Ralston and others. If you do not qualify, ask your teacher about uBEATS. It is an online alternative. Questions: 402-559-3027.
duration: Whole school year, August to May
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page. Students get three polo shirts and a jacket free and buy their own black pants, socks and closed-toe shoes.

who_can_apply: Students ages 13 to 26 can help with Pediatric Programs. Students 16 and older can also help with Adult Programs.
how_to_apply: Email the volunteer coordinator. Their name is on the page. Then finish the required training.
notes: Training is on behavior and disability. It is on play and safety too. The institute also lists job shadowing for high school students.
duration: Opportunities are year-round. Camp Munroe runs in quarterly cycles: spring, summer, fall and winter.
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: High school juniors or seniors (when applying) with at least a 2.0 GPA on a 4.0 scale. You must show you want to be a leader after you finish school.
how_to_apply: Apply online. Upload your unofficial high school transcript. Send one letter of recommendation. Write an essay of at least 300 words about two goals for the next five years.
notes: The same page also lists UNO Jumpstart. It is a 2 week program for graduating seniors who are already UNO students.
duration: The 2026 session ran May 26 to June 26, 2026.
pay_detail: Free. Tuition, fees, books and parking permits are covered for selected students.

who_can_apply: Lifeguard I: at least 15 years old with an 8th grade education. You also need the city's Starguard lifeguard certification. Lifeguard II is 16 and up with one year of experience in Overland Park. Lifeguard III is 17 and up with two years.
how_to_apply: The job description does not say how to apply. It requires Starguard certification from the City of Overland Park. The course is the Starguard Lifeguard Course.
notes: Quote from the job description: a minimum of 15 years of age. The job description does not state pay. Current postings and pay were not on the program page.
duration: Seasonal. Exact season dates not stated on the job description.
pay_detail: Not stated on the job description

who_can_apply: Students in grades 9 to 12, described on the page as 14 to 17 years old. Up to 25 teens are picked.
how_to_apply: Register online. Then do an interview. Bring a letter of recommendation. Or bring references from someone outside your family. Call 701.277.9240 to ask about the next trimester.
notes: Up to six teens work each shift.
duration: Trimesters during the school year. Saturdays and Sundays, 9 am to 2 pm. At least two 4.5 hour shifts a month, up to four.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Teens pay $125 per trimester for zoo members or $175 per trimester for non-members.

who_can_apply: High school students ages 16 to 18 (or finished 10th grade by June 12). Need a 3.0 GPA and a health screening that shows immunizations.
how_to_apply: You need an application signed by you and a parent or guardian. You need a school counselor form. You need one adult reference who is not a relative. You also need a parental consent form. Apply online or mail the paper form. Email BO-VOLUNTEERS@sarmc.org with questions.
notes: Applications for the 2027 session open March 1, 2027. This is from the requirements page.
duration: Summer session (2026 ran through the summer until August 14, after an orientation the week of May 25)
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer work.

who_can_apply: Adults and students ages 14 and older.
how_to_apply: Complete the application. Then take part in an interview. The Volunteer Services Coordinator is Diedre Schmelzer. Call 208-205-0292.
notes: Ask about teen placements when you call.
duration: Not stated on the program page
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer work.

who_can_apply: Volunteers must be at least 16 years old. Some jobs need you to be 18 or 19. The page lists more than 20 jobs open to 16 year olds.
how_to_apply: Submit the online application. Then do a phone interview and a criminal background check. You also need an updated vaccination record. Next come a one hour orientation with a health assessment. Then come a department orientation. Call Volunteer Services. The number is (605) 333-6374.
notes: No special program for 14 and 15 year olds was found on this page. Some roles need a vaccination record and a background check, so start early.
duration: A weekly or biweekly shift of three to four hours for medical center, clinic and wellness center volunteers.
pay_detail: Unpaid.

who_can_apply: Junior Camp Counselors are 14 to 18. General volunteers must be at least 14, pass a background check, sign a waiver and finish onboarding.
how_to_apply: Apply through the volunteer portal. Questions go to volunteer@sciowa.org.
notes: The exact opening day in February 2027 is not posted. Questions? Email volunteer@sciowa.org.
duration: Two weeks required, Monday to Friday 8:30 am to 4:30 pm. Onboarding with staff comes before any volunteer role.
pay_detail: Unpaid. After 40 hours of service the position description says you get a free one-year membership.

who_can_apply: Must be at least 15 years of age to work for SFPR Aquatics. For the course, you must be 15 on the last day of class.
how_to_apply: Sign up for the lifeguard class on the city page. Call (605) 367-POOL with questions.
notes: The 15 year minimum comes from the certification page, and you must be 15 on the last day of the class. The city says finishing the course does not guarantee a job.
duration: Course runs Friday to Sunday. Job length not stated on the program page.
pay_detail: Paid job. Pay rate not stated on the program page. The course costs $185 per person, or it is free if you commit to work for SFPR.

who_can_apply: Volunteers must be age 14 or older and have finished 7th grade, with a parent's consent if under 18. Teen Advisory Board members must have finished 7th grade and be in public, private or home school.
how_to_apply: Print the volunteer form, get a parent to sign if you are under 18, and take it to any branch. Join the Teen Advisory Board when the next form opens.
notes: The library says it may not be able to place every volunteer. Court-ordered community service is not accepted on the form. Advisory Board meetings are at the Caille Branch, 4100 S. Carnegie Cir., first Monday of the month, 4:30 to 5:30 p.m. Next Teen Advisory Board dates are not posted; the 2026-27 cycle is closed.
duration: Advisory Board meets once a month for one hour, Oct 5, 2026 to May 3, 2027. General volunteer time is set with the branch.
pay_detail: Unpaid. The Teen Advisory Board page says meetings 'qualify for volunteer hours'.

who_can_apply: Registered 4-H member in good standing, age 14 to 18 based on the 4-H year. The page lists no grade rule.
how_to_apply: Send the application form, a personal narrative and two letters of recommendation. Then interview at the State Fair. You can do it in person or online.
notes: Ambassadors must already be registered 4-H members. Costs for the orientation, retreat and events are not stated on the program page. Questions: call 605-688-4792.
duration: A full year of duties. The page does not give a term length.
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 24 and allowed to work in the US. Live in South Dakota or a nearby county. In-school youth ages 14 to 21 must be low-income and have a barrier such as basic skills deficient, English learner, homeless, in foster care, pregnant or parenting, or have a disability. Out-of-school youth must be 16 to 24.
how_to_apply: Call 605-773-3101 (TTY 711) to ask where to start. Under 18, a parent or guardian must sign the application forms.
notes: Narrow: not every teen qualifies. The state may limit how many in-school youth it enrolls because at least 75 percent of funds go to out-of-school youth. Rules are from the state WIOA manual, section 4.1, revised October 2026. The state says all Title I youth also sign up for Wagner-Peyser job services. The manual also lists Selective Service registration rules (policy 4.6) that this card does not cover.
duration: Not stated on the program page.
pay_detail: Not stated on the program pages. The manual says the program is not an entitlement and depends on funding.

who_can_apply: Must be at least 16 before the program starts in January. The page does not state a maximum age. Minimum 3.0 GPA. Boise campus only. The program cannot take new volunteers past their junior year of high school.
how_to_apply: Submit an online application when it opens in November. Call (208) 381-2265 with questions. You must also finish orientation and service training. You must attend quarterly meetings. You also need proof of immunizations (MMR, varicella, Tdap, T-spot and a current flu shot).
notes: The opening date of Nov 2 is worked out from the page rule. The rule says the first Monday in November. The date is not printed on the page.
duration: 8 hours a month during the school year and 12 hours a month in June, July and August
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer work.

who_can_apply: Volunteers must be at least 13 years old or accompanied by an adult while on duty.
how_to_apply: Fill out the volunteer application on the library website. You may be interviewed. Volunteers are chosen by their qualifications. The library's needs at the time also count. Call or email the volunteer contact listed on the page with questions.
notes: Quote from the volunteer policy: Volunteers must be at least 13 years old or accompanied by an adult while on duty. The page links to a separate Teen Volunteer path. This card does not cover it in detail.
duration: Not stated on the program page
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Students in grades 5 to 12. Please RSVP before attending.
how_to_apply: RSVP, then pay online from the zoo page. A scholarship form is there too.
notes: This is a club, not a job. Meets at the Gary K. Clarke Education Center at the zoo, entering through the front admission gate.
duration: 1st and 3rd Tuesday of the month, 5:15 to 6:45 pm, during the school year
pay_detail: $125 per student for the whole school year (includes a t-shirt). A scholarship fund application is linked on the page.

who_can_apply: High school students. No grade or age rule is listed on the program page.
how_to_apply: The program page does not explain the steps. Email sdd@uidaho.edu or call 208-885-1186.
notes: Full refunds were offered only through June 11 in 2026. Check the page next spring for new dates and prices.
duration: 4 days (June 24 to 27 in 2026)
pay_detail: $450, or $425 for returning campers. It covers workshops, supplies, room and board. Local students who go home at night can email sdd@uidaho.edu for a different price.

who_can_apply: Montana high school students. The page says sophomores and juniors during the 2025-2026 school year. That wording may be old, so ask the program contact about your grade.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply here form on the program page when it opens. Questions: Annie Zavitz at Annie.Zavitz@mso.umt.edu.
notes: Students live in residence halls and share meals. No closing date is posted, so apply as soon as the form opens.
duration: 2 weeks (July 5 to 16, 2027)
pay_detail: Free. A US Department of Education grant pays the cost.

who_can_apply: The page says 'Be 14-18 years of age or older' and 'Currently enrolled in high school'.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online volunteer application. Then do a placement interview and orientation. Other steps are a handbook review, state and national background checks, a health screening, an annual flu shot and a TB test. Email DM_Volunteers@unitypoint.org or call (515) 263-5227.
notes: This card is for Iowa Lutheran Hospital only. Other UnityPoint hospitals in Des Moines have their own volunteer pages; teen rules for them were not read. The health screening, flu shot and TB test take time, so start early.
duration: Set number of hours not stated for teens.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Volunteers can earn silver cord hours for graduation.

who_can_apply: In 2026: high school students entering their senior year and 2026 high school graduates. The page says the 2027 details will be updated later.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. You fill out a separate scholarship application too. Got a question? Call 406-243-2537. Or send a note to bethany.applegate@umontana.edu.
notes: Students earn two college credits. The page says to check back in early 2027 for updated information and the application.
duration: About 10 days (2026 dates: June 10 to 19)
pay_detail: 2026 cost: $2,800 for tuition, course fees, housing, all meals and program costs. Scholarships are worth about 10 to 50 percent of the cost and need a separate application.

who_can_apply: Current 10th graders at a public or private high school in Wyoming or homeschooled, who live in Wyoming and plan to return to a Wyoming school. Must stay all three weeks.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online student application. It needs a personal statement. This is an essay of at least 300 words or a video of no more than 4 minutes. It also needs an awards and achievements list and a recommendation letter. Your counselor uploads your transcript.
notes: The how-to-apply page says HSI 2027 applications open October 1 and all pieces are due February 7, 2027. Wyoming students only.
duration: Three weeks in June (the exact 2027 dates are not stated on the program pages)
pay_detail: Room, board and supplies are paid by funds from the Wyoming Legislature. There is a $325 activity fee. Travel and personal spending are on the student.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 15 to 18 who can travel to the central meeting place each day. Housing is not provided.
how_to_apply: Use the Tacoma apply link on the page. Ask about tuition help.
notes: Crews may earn high school credit if your school agrees. The same program also runs in Eugene, OR and Boise, ID.
duration: 5 weeks, Monday to Friday (2026: June 22 to July 24 and July 28 to Aug 28)
pay_detail: Stipend of $96 a day (up to $480 a week) plus $20 weekly dependability bonus and $20 weekly safety bonus. $200 tuition, with tuition help based on need.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 18.
how_to_apply: The event page does not say if you need to sign up. Call the museum at 316-268-4921 to ask.
notes: It is at the Wichita Art Museum, 1400 West Museum Boulevard. The event page does not say whether sign-up is required.
duration: One evening, 6 to 8 p.m.
pay_detail: Free.

who_can_apply: Must be at least 14 years old unless an event says something different. Volunteers 16 and older must pass a background check.
how_to_apply: All volunteers must go through an application process. Then sign up for a shift on the volunteer calendar. To apply to be a gallery docent, use the application link on the program page. Call the volunteer coordinator at 316-660-0603.
notes: Special events can have their own age rules. The page says volunteers 16 and older must complete a background check.
duration: Pick shifts from the volunteer calendar. The page does not state a minimum time.
pay_detail: Volunteer role.

who_can_apply: High school students. The page does not list other eligibility rules.
how_to_apply: Use the printable flyer on the page. The museum's general number is 316-265-9314.
notes: The page says the program is in its third year. Last Teen Night dates listed were April 5, 2025 and April 11, 2026. The school flyer needs principal approval before it is handed out.
duration: Meets once a month from October. The Teen Night event is in April.
pay_detail: Unpaid. The page calls it a good way to earn volunteer hours.

who_can_apply: The Teen Advisory Board is open to teens in grades 6 to 12. The program page does not give a grade rule for the Summer Reading volunteers.
how_to_apply: For the Teen Advisory Board, email the teen librarian named on the page. Watch the same page for the next Summer Reading Volunteer application.
notes: The Summer Reading volunteer program has run since 1990, says the page. The library's main Volunteer page lists other volunteer options.
duration: Teen Advisory Board: one meeting a month at the Advanced Learning Library. Summer Reading volunteers: during the summer program.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Members earn volunteer hours. Summer Reading teens can earn more than 30 hours.

who_can_apply: Sedgwick County residents between ages 7 and 19. You can enroll if you turn 7 before January 1 of the 4-H year. If you turn 19 before January 1, you cannot enroll.
how_to_apply: Call 316-660-0115 to find clubs near you. Then enroll online in Kansas 4-H.
notes: The same page also says 4-H is for ages 5 to 18, and it names a county fair deadline for a different county. To show in the county fair 4-H division, join by May 1. Call the Sedgwick office to confirm.
duration: The 4-H year runs Oct 1 to Sep 30.
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Age 14 or older for special events. For some events, volunteers under 18 must come with an adult. Husbandry aide volunteers must be 18.
how_to_apply: Use the Get Started link on the volunteer page to contact the zoo, complete a volunteer application, and go to a volunteer orientation (2nd Saturday 8 to 10 a.m. or 4th Thursday 4 to 6 p.m. at the Cargill Learning Center).
notes: Quote from the page: Must be 14 years of age to volunteer for Special Events. Groups can do service days in the zoo departments from age 16, scheduled two weeks ahead, April through October. Adults 18 and over must pass a background check.
duration: Event by event, spread through the year
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Applicants must be 16 or older. Wesley does not take volunteers for court-ordered hours, and it does not offer one-time or group volunteering.
how_to_apply: Download the volunteer application and fill it out. Then mail it to Wesley Volunteer Services, 550 N. Hillside St., Wichita, KS 67214, or scan and email it. Next come a personal interview and a criminal background check. Then you submit personal health records and go to orientation.
notes: Quote from the page: Applicants must be 16 years of age or older. Volunteers must keep up a regular schedule. A mandatory flu shot policy applies in flu season.
duration: At least 4 shifts a month and 60 total hours, which the page says takes about six months
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Students in grades 4 to 12. The page lists the grades for each camp. Two 2026 camps were for grades 9 to 12.
how_to_apply: Use the registration link on the program page. Use the scholarship form on the same page to ask for help with cost.
notes: In 2026 the Biomedical Engineering camp ran June 22 to 26. Ethical Hacking ran July 13 to 17.
duration: Most camps last 1 week in June and July
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page. Scholarships are available through a form on the page.

who_can_apply: Kansas high school students, or eighth graders who are about to start high school. You must be first in your family to go to college (neither parent in the home has a bachelor's degree). Or your family income must be within federal rules. You should like math, science, engineering or health jobs.
how_to_apply: Tell your school counselor you are interested, or call Upward Bound Math Science at 316-978-3316.
notes: Application deadlines, cost and pay are Not stated on the program page.
duration: 6 weeks in June and July
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 15 to 17. Classes are at several YMCA branches and Wichita high schools. Newton picks 15 students based on birthdate and location.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online enrollment form. Or use a printable form from the page and turn it in at your YMCA branch front desk. You can also email the Job Prep contact on the page.
notes: Spots are limited. The page names past summer job sites. They include the Sedgwick County Zoo, the Wichita Art Museum and Exploration Place. They also include Wesley Medical Center and Wichita Habitat for Humanity. The page says over 350 summer jobs were offered. The Workforce Alliance YEP page also points teens to this program.
duration: Class once a week for 2 hours, February to May
pay_detail: The course is free. The summer job is the reward; the program page does not state the pay.

who_can_apply: Workshops are open to anyone age 14 and older. Work experience placements need you to be at least 16 by June 1 of that year. The workforce centers are in Wichita, El Dorado, Wellington and Arkansas City. Some employers only place ages 18 and older.
how_to_apply: Make a KANSASWORKS account. Then fill out the YEP registration form. Once it is on file, you are sent information to sign up for workshops and job fairs. Age 14 to 17: bring a non-expired picture ID and birth certificate, plus a signed Social Security card, for a work placement.
notes: Camp HYPE is listed for age 15. The FAQ also points to the City of Wichita Way to Work program and the YMCA Job Prep program. A different Workforce Alliance program, WIOA Youth, is for out-of-school youth ages 16 to 24 with barriers and an income limit.
duration: Workshops March to June. Most jobs run June to August.
pay_detail: Placements pay at least $7.25 per hour. Workshops do not pay. Most placements are 20 hours a week or less and last 8 weeks or less.

who_can_apply: Ages 12 to 15 at the start of camp. Separate Girls Camp and Boys Camp weeks. Residency rules are not stated on the program page.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply link on the camps page when it opens. Questions: Parker Everhart, parker.everhart@wyo.gov, 307-823-2368.
notes: Ages 12 to 15 only, so older teens should look at other cards.
duration: About one week (2026: Boys Camp June 14 to 20, Girls Camp July 5 to 11)
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page. The camps are funded in partnership with the Wyldlife Fund.

who_can_apply: In-school youth ages 14 to 21, or out-of-school youth ages 16 to 24. Must live in Wyoming and meet low-income rules or have another qualifying barrier to work.
how_to_apply: Contact your local Workforce Center to see if you qualify.
notes: Out-of-school youth can join up to age 24. Eligibility rules vary, so ask your local Workforce Center.
duration: Not stated on the program page
pay_detail: The page lists "paid or unpaid" work experience and training. Pay rates are not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 15 to 18 at the time of their orientation session. You must be able to attend one weekend orientation.
how_to_apply: Teens or parents can ask for information. To do that, send an email to the zoo. The address is education@zoomontana.org.
notes: The page does not say what year it is for. Email the zoo to ask when the next orientation is.
duration: One orientation plus at least one five-day camp
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page (the page describes it as a chance to learn job skills and leadership).
